awards_draft#u3.description: Current 2026-27 eligibility details (20-minute definition, two 15-20 minute allowance) and positionless All-NBA ballot rules are from memory of the 2023 CBA and have not been re-read in the 2026-27 league rulebook. Which awards the rule governs (and that it does not govern monthly awards, Coach or Executive of the Year, All-Star selection or draft markets) is likewise unverified.
awards_draft#u3.what_would_resolve: Read the league's published award criteria for the 2026-27 season and confirm each threshold.
awards_draft#u3.classification_rationale: Verified via 2026 reporting: eligibility = 65 games (20+ min in 63, 15-20 min allowed in two more), covering MVP, DPOY, MIP, All-NBA and All-Defense; ROY, Sixth Man and All-Rookie exempt (secondary source). Also verified: an 'extraordinary circumstances' appeal to an NBA/NBPA-designated expert can grant eligibility (Doncic and Cunningham granted, Edwards denied, 2025-26). The record has no appeal stage, so eligibility is not a pure ledger gate.
awards_draft#u3.catalog_action: Add an appeal stage (filing and grant probability) to nba.games_played_eligibility / nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger in awards_draft, and record the verified list of governed awards (MVP, DPOY, MIP, All-NBA, All-Defense) with exemptions.

awards_draft#u5.description: The All-Star formula weights (50/25/25), the five-starter and seven-reserve split by position group per conference, wildcard rules and the availability of historical early-return fan-vote snapshots are from memory of recent seasons and have not been checked against the 2027 rules or a machine-readable archive.
awards_draft#u5.what_would_resolve: Read the league's published All-Star selection rules for 2027 and check whether early-return snapshots exist in a machine-readable archive.
awards_draft#u5.classification_rationale: Verified for 2026: starters 50% fans / 25% players / 25% media; coaches pick 7 reserves per conference regardless of position (positionless); the USA-vs-World format needs 16 US and 8 international All-Stars, with the Commissioner adding players to fill the quotas. The record's position-group split is wrong, and the nationality quota plus Commissioner additions are a selection stage it lacks.
awards_draft#u5.catalog_action: In awards_draft, rewrite nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote to positionless selection and add a nationality-quota/Commissioner-addition stage with a player nationality input. Mark the 2027 format as pending until the league announces it.

awards_draft#u6.description: The Hustle Award (KXNBAHUSTLE) is decided from tracked hustle statistics (deflections, charges, loose balls, screen assists, contests) and no input here aggregates them; the Teammate and Sportsmanship player votes are carried only by the generic nominee model, so these three remain thinly modelled.
awards_draft#u6.what_would_resolve: Create dedicated archetypes (Hall of Fame election, All-Star Weekend events, season stat leader) or confirm the existing season_stat_markets record defines stat-leader inputs.
awards_draft#u6.classification_rationale: The Hustle Award is chosen by formula from tracked hustle stats (deflections, charges drawn, loose balls, screen assists, contests). No catalog input aggregates those stats, so the KXNBAHUSTLE mechanism has no driver. This is a missing input, not a magnitude.
awards_draft#u6.catalog_action: Author an nba.hustle_stat_index input (league hustle-stats endpoint, award formula weights) and attach it to KXNBAHUSTLE in awards_draft. Keep Teammate and Sportsmanship on the generic nominee model.

off_court_events#u4.description: Expansion, European-league and conference-realignment markets have linked voting and negotiation dynamics (expansion in two cities forces realignment of one or two Western teams to the East) that the governance pipeline treats as separate events; the dependence between KXNBACITYEXPAND, KXNBAJOINCONF and KXNBAEUROPEANNOUNCE is not modelled.
off_court_events#u4.what_would_resolve: Build a joint scenario tree for expansion, realignment and European-league decisions from league statements and board calendars.
off_court_events#u4.classification_rationale: Expansion awards, conference realignment (two new Western cities force teams East) and a European-league announcement are causally linked board decisions. The record prices KXNBACITYEXPAND, KXNBAJOINCONF and KXNBAEUROPEANNOUNCE as independent events. A joint dependence structure is missing, not just unmeasured.
off_court_events#u4.catalog_action: Author a joint governance scenario input (expansion award -> realignment -> European announcement, keyed to board calendars) in off_court_events. Wire the three series to it in place of independent hazards.

parlay_combo#u7.classification_rationale: KXNBANHL needs a Stanley Cup probability, and no NBA input defines or references one. The cross-sport link (input id, as-of alignment) is missing from the record.
parlay_combo#u7.catalog_action: Link the NHL catalog's Stanley Cup title input by id with as-of timestamp alignment (or define a shared cross-sport input) and attach it to KXNBANHL in parlay_combo.

player_availability#u2.what_would_resolve: Check whether game-level starter or active markets are listed during the season and re-file accordingly.

quarter_and_half_markets#qh-2h-ot-split.description: Each text is explicit (KXNBA2H, KXNBA2HSPREAD and KXNBA2HTOTAL include overtime; KXNBA2HWINNER says the 2nd half 'does not include overtime'), so this is not a wording gap; what is open is that one simulated game must yield both a regulation-only and an OT-inclusive second-half margin, and no input states how the two are produced jointly.
quarter_and_half_markets#qh-2h-ot-split.what_would_resolve: Define the OT-inclusive 2H margin as regulation 2H margin plus an OT increment drawn from nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin, and check settled KXNBA2H and KXNBA2HWINNER markets from one overtime game.
quarter_and_half_markets#qh-2h-ot-split.classification_rationale: The texts are explicit: KXNBA2H, 2HSPREAD and 2HTOTAL include OT, and 2HWINNER excludes it. No input defines how one simulated game yields both the regulation-only and the OT-inclusive 2H margin, so that definition is missing.
quarter_and_half_markets#qh-2h-ot-split.catalog_action: In quarter_and_half_markets, define the OT-inclusive 2H margin as regulation 2H margin plus an OT increment from nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin, and map KXNBA2HWINNER and KXNBA2H to the two outputs.

quarter_and_half_markets#qh-live-state.description: Q2, Q3, Q4 and 2H markets exist for the same game as Q1, and the sampled rules give no close or trading-stop time. If they trade after tipoff, the needed inputs include in-game state (score at period start, who is on court, foul and bonus state, time remaining), which no input here covers; if they close at tipoff, pregame information suffices.
quarter_and_half_markets#qh-live-state.what_would_resolve: Read the market close_time and trading hours for later-period markets on a live event and check whether quotes move after the first tip; then add a live-state input set if they do.
quarter_and_half_markets#qh-live-state.classification_rationale: Checked live via the Kalshi API: KXNBA2H-26NOV07SASPOR markets have close_time 05:35Z, after the game ended, with early close 'after a winner is declared'. Later-period markets trade in play, so in-game state inputs are required and the record has none.
quarter_and_half_markets#qh-live-state.catalog_action: Author a live-state input set in quarter_and_half_markets (score at period start, clock, on-court lineups, team-foul/bonus state from cdn.nba.com liveData) and attach it to the Q2-Q4 and 2H series.

season_futures_team#sf-tiebreak-and-divi.what_would_resolve: Code the league's 2026-27 tiebreak document into nba.tiebreak_ledger, test on past tied divisions and mark nba.division_race_tiebreak_state DUPLICATE_OF it in the catalog.

season_futures_team#sf-tiebreak-and-divi.catalog_action: Mark nba.division_race_tiebreak_state DUPLICATE_OF nba.tiebreak_ledger in the NBA catalog, and code the 2026-27 league tiebreak procedure into nba.tiebreak_ledger for season_futures_team.

season_stat_markets#ss-ownership-overlap.catalog_action: Define one shared regular-season path simulation input referenced by season_futures_team and season_stat_markets, and record nba.team_win_streak_hazard and nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model as views of it.

series_and_cup#sc-archetype-mismatch.catalog_action: Decide and record in series_and_cup whether Cup contracts move to their own archetype (with nba.cup_format, nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state) and file the comeback/blowout series with in-game score inputs.

series_and_cup#sc-cup-bracket-structure.description: nba.cup_finals_pair_probability assumes the Cup knockout bracket is split by conference so the Finals pair is one East and one West team, with semifinals and final at one neutral site; the current season's bracket, seeding of wildcards and venue rules are not verified here, and a shared site adds correlation the product formula ignores.
series_and_cup#sc-cup-bracket-structure.what_would_resolve: Read the league's 2026-27 Cup format document and record bracket halves, wildcard seeding and venues; bound the pair probability under a copula.
series_and_cup#sc-cup-bracket-structure.classification_rationale: Verified for 2026-27: three group winners plus one wild card per conference make conference-split quarterfinals. Semifinals are now at the higher seed's arena and only the final is neutral, at Hinkle Fieldhouse, Indianapolis. The record wrongly gives the semifinal zero home advantage and models a shared semifinal site.
series_and_cup#sc-cup-bracket-structure.catalog_action: In series_and_cup, update nba.cup_finals_pair_probability and nba.cup_format: home-court for the higher seed in the semifinal, no shared-venue copula, neutral final at Hinkle Fieldhouse, and wild card = best second-place team per conference.
